page: Microsoft Azure E16-8as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the EASv5 series. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz across 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs, configured with two threads per core under Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU allocation of 16.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache provisions include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. The instance features no included local storage and contains no discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data reflects strong single-core computational output alongside moderate multi-threaded efficiency. In CPU stress testing, the instance scores 2,702.79 on single-core stress-ng operations, placing it in the top 25 percent of tested machines, while multi-core stress-ng reaches 10,800.25 within the average tier. Memory subsystem testing shows read speeds of 516.37 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 39.4 GB/sec for larger 256 MB uncached reads. However, uncached 256 MB write throughput drops to 22.29 GB/sec, placing it in the lower quartile. In application-focused metrics, it sustains 8.24 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves a PassMark database score of 3,577.97.

The constrained core count paired with a large memory footprint offers a cost-effective design for workloads where licensing fees depend on CPU core counts but working sets demand significant memory capacity. The absence of built-in local NVMe storage requires external disk attachments for persistent state. As a result, the E16-8as_v5 is primarily suited for large in-memory caches, enterprise relational databases, memory-resident analytics, and intermediate caching layers that do not require intensive parallel CPU throughput.
description: Microsoft Azure E16-8as_v5 is a memory-optimized instance featuring an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.525 GHz, delivering 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores and 128.0 GB of system memory. This architecture yields a high 16.0 GB per-vCPU ratio, accompanied by 32 MB of L3 cache, with no local storage or attached GPUs. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong single-core processing capabilities, scoring 2,702.79 in stress-ng single-core tests, alongside steady Redis throughput of 8.24 million SET operations per second. While uncached large-block write throughput is relatively constrained at 22.29 GB/sec, the instance's high RAM density per CPU core presents an efficient profile for software deployments governed by per-core licensing. The configuration is well suited for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including relational database engines, Redis caching, and in-memory data processing.
